prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1248; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from insured's side regarding a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Reported vehicle damage to rear bumper and trunk area. Claimant reports neck and back strain, has not yet sought treatment. Advised claimant of medical payments coverage and rental reimbursement options. Claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from claimant. Claimant states they were stopped at a red light when their vehicle was struck from behind. Describes sudden jolt, immediate neck stiffness, and lower back pain by the following day. Police report number on file. Photos of claimant vehicle received and attached to file.

Entry 3: Contacted other driver's carrier to confirm liability coverage and policy limits. Liability accepted on preliminary review based on police narrative and vehicle damage pattern. Other driver's statement consistent with following too closely. Requested written confirmation of coverage for the file.

Entry 4: Claimant provided medical records from initial urgent care visit showing diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain, with prescribed muscle relaxants and physical therapy referral. Claimant still unrepresented; reminded claimant they may consult an attorney and that this adjuster cannot give legal advice. Reviewing treatment plan against typical recovery timelines for soft tissue injuries.

Entry 5: Physical therapy progress notes received showing improved range of motion. Claimant reports pain has decreased but still intermittent. Repair estimate reviewed and approved for bumper replacement and trunk panel work. Rental extended pending repair completion. File set for follow-up review once treatment concludes.
